pages.title: Courses
pages.content:
Four ways into the cab: Class C+E for articulated lorries (6 days, from £1,640), Class C for rigid lorries (6 days, £1,890), a one-to-one Refresher day (6 hours, £340) and the Driver CPC periodic week (35 hours, £395).

Every course includes the lorry for the test and a warm-up drive. Two trainees share each lorry each day, and every lesson starts with the walk-round.

pages.title: Class C+E
pages.content: Class C+E is for Class C holders who want to drive an articulated lorry. Five training days and the test day on a tractor unit with a 13.6 m curtain-side trailer: £1,640. The C then C+E pathway, ten training days and two test days, is £3,380.

pages.title: Class C
pages.content: Class C is the rigid lorry licence. Five training days and the test day in an 18-tonne rigid: £1,890. The next intake starts on 12 January 2027.

pages.title: The yard weeks
pages.content:
Seven weeks from enrolment to test day: assessment drive in week 0, medical and theory in weeks 1 to 2, theory tests passed and the test date confirmed in week 3, yard week in week 4, road days in week 5, a mock test in week 6 and the practical test in week 7.

A typical yard day runs daily to the same routine: walk-round at 07:30, manoeuvres at 08:00, road at 10:30, lunch at 12:30, reversing exercise at 13:15, debrief at 16:00 and close at 17:00.

pages.title: Fees & dates
pages.content:
Assessment drive £120 (deducted from a course booked within 30 days), theory coaching £90, Class C course £1,890, Class C+E course £1,640, C then C+E pathway £3,380, Refresher day £340, Driver CPC periodic week £395.

Intakes in 2027: 12 January, 9 March, 11 May, 6 July, 14 September and 9 November, twelve places each.

pages.title: Test day
pages.content:
We book your practical test for week 7 on the day you enrol. The morning starts with a warm-up drive in our lorry, then the practical test: vehicle safety questions, the reversing exercise and an on-road drive.

If you do not pass, the retest package is a one-to-one Refresher day at £340 with a retest within ten working days.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
Kamotsu Academy was founded in 2009 by Ruth Abernethy, a former fuel tanker driver, with one second-hand rigid lorry in a rented bay at Hollins Freight Park, Ashby Vale.

Today the academy runs five lorries from a 1.4-hectare yard, with five instructors and two trainees per lorry per day.

pages.title: Fleet & yard
pages.content:
Five lorries: three 18-tonne rigids for Class C and two tractor units with 13.6 m curtain-side trailers for Class C+E.

The 1.4-hectare yard has a reversing bay, a coupling bay and two classrooms.

posts.title: Leila: from the picking aisle to the C+E cab
posts.content:
Leila Haddad spent six years as a warehouse picker before she booked an assessment drive. She remembers the first walk-round: the checklist felt longer than the drive.

By week 4 the walk-round was a habit. She coupled her first trailer in the yard with Ilse Brandt watching from the side, and passed her practical test in week 7.

“The checklist stops being a list,” she says. “It becomes the way you look at a lorry.”

posts.title: Marcus: a bus driver learns the reversing bay
posts.content:
Marcus Bell drove a passenger bus for fifteen years. Adding Class C meant learning a different kind of reversing: no mirrors on the left, a long box behind him and a bay marked in cones.

Daniel Moreau had him walk the bay before he drove it. Two trainees per lorry meant long stretches of cab time, and by the end of the yard week the bay was no longer the hard part.

posts.title: Sofia: ten years away, one refresher day
posts.content:
Sofia Ferreira drove lorries until 2016, then spent ten years away from the cab. A one-to-one refresher day was enough to get her back.

She started with the walk-round, checked the tread on each tyre with a gauge, and spent the afternoon on the road with her instructor. “It felt like a long time away, until I was back in the seat.”

posts.title: 2027 intake dates and open yard Saturdays
posts.content:
The 2027 intakes start on 12 January, 9 March, 11 May, 6 July, 14 September and 9 November, with twelve places each.

The yard is open to visitors on the first Saturday of each month from 09:00 to 12:00. Come and sit in a cab and meet the instructors.
